profiles.name: Loyal Regulars
profiles.note: Buys often and recently, mid-to-high spend.
profiles.recommendation: Consider a loyalty programme and replenishment reminders based on past purchase timing.

profiles.name: Big-Basket Buyers
profiles.note: Fewer orders, but large quantities / order values.
profiles.recommendation: Consider bulk / bundle options and clear stock-availability information.

profiles.name: Dormant / At-Risk
profiles.note: Has not purchased for a long time.
profiles.recommendation: Consider a single win-back message; if there is no response, stop contacting and review list hygiene.

insights.title: Highest-revenue segment
insights.detail: Loyal Regulars (cluster 1) contributes 80.04% of revenue from 1198 customers.
insights.action: Consider a loyalty programme and replenishment reminders based on past purchase timing.

insights.title: Most frequent segment
insights.detail: Loyal Regulars averages 10.23 orders per customer.
insights.action: Consider a loyalty programme and replenishment reminders based on past purchase timing.

insights.title: Dormant customers
insights.detail: 1163 customers (26.81%) are in the dormant profile.
insights.action: Consider win-back only for this group, and measure response before repeating.

insights.title: Spending is uneven across segments
insights.detail: Average spend ranges from £250 to £5,954 per customer. A single offer for all customers would miss that spread.
insights.action: Consider segment-specific offers rather than one blanket promotion.

pca.note: PCA is for visualisation only; clustering was run on the scaled RFM feature space, not on these two components. A 2-D projection can distort distances.

metric_notes.silhouette: Higher is better (-1 to 1); only valid with >=2 clusters.
metric_notes.davies_bouldin: Lower is better; ratio of within-cluster scatter to separation.
metric_notes.calinski_harabasz: Higher is better; ratio of between- to within-cluster dispersion.
metric_notes.aic_bic: GMM only. Lower AIC/BIC is better; they are model-selection criteria, not clustering metrics.
